description: Gold-standard Level-3 ruleset for NDAs. Situations are infinite; this maps them onto a FINITE feature set and writes deterministic rules over those features. The AI's only job is to fill these features from the user's free-text situation (the interview); the rules below — authored and reviewed by lawyers — decide the document.

feature_taxonomy.note: Who is receiving the information — the single biggest driver of clause shape.
Formulae, processes, methods with independent economic value.
Personal data of Indian residents (DPDP Act 2023 trigger).

baseline_clauses.why: Parties must be identified for any enforceable contract.
Defined terms used throughout the agreement.
Confidential Information must be defined to be enforceable.
The core confidentiality obligation (default; may be upgraded by a rule).
Standard carve-outs (public domain, prior knowledge, legal compulsion).
Controls on onward disclosure to third parties.
Security measures protecting the confidential information.
Return / destruction of information on termination.
Confidentiality must be time-limited; perpetual NDAs risk unenforceability.

rules.why: Trade secrets require the highest grade of confidentiality and survive longer.
rules.legal_basis: ICA s.27; IT Act 2000 s.43A; ICA s.73

rules.why: Investor / diligence counterparties get heightened, need-to-know confidentiality with non-use for competing/investment advantage.
rules.note: Lower priority than R1 — if both trade secrets AND investor, trade-secret grade wins.

rules.why: Source code needs no-copy / no-reverse-engineer / no-derivative protection.
rules.legal_basis: Copyright Act 1957 s.2(o), s.14; IT Act 2000 s.43

rules.why: Dedicated non-use / account-for-gains obligation over trade secrets.
Vendor/supplier counterparties: protect business contacts from circumvention.
Personal data of Indian residents triggers DPDP-aligned data-processing obligations.
Optional narrow non-compete tied to confidential information.
rules.legal_basis: ICA s.27 — enforceable only if narrowly tied to CI

fallback_policy.principle: Open-world, honest degradation. If a situation has aspects not covered by the feature taxonomy or rules, generate the baseline NDA and tell the user — never silently guess.
fallback_policy.review_message: This NDA covers aspects we don't yet have a specific rule for. We recommend a lawyer review before relying on it.
fallback_policy.learning: Recurring uncovered signals should be promoted into new features/rules here, with legal review — this is how coverage grows over time.

execution_note: This ruleset is the canonical, human-reviewable source of truth. It currently maps 1:1 onto knowledge-base/clause_library/blueprints/nda.blueprint.json (variant_clauses ↔ replace rules, conditional_clauses ↔ add rules). The blueprint is what the engine executes; this file is what a lawyer reviews and what other document types should be modelled on.
